themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints in Central Harlem spiked to 45 this week—a 143% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 18.5 per week—signaling a rapid deterioration in pest control across the district this week.
evidence: 45 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 18.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (143% spike, z-score: 4.27)
Spike coincides with ongoing street sanitation and disposal complaint increases (9 residential disposal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.1 avg)
Dead animal complaints also up 500% last week (3 vs. 0.5 avg), suggesting systemic waste management breakdown
reporting_angles: Interview affected residents in high-complaint blocks; map complaints to identify hotspots and inadequate waste pickup routes
Investigate whether recent street/residential sanitation staffing changes or service cuts triggered the cascade

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints exploded to 5 last week—a 471% increase from the 8-week baseline of 0.9 per week—suggesting coordinated tree removal or damage activity across Central Harlem last week.
evidence: 5 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (471% spike, z-score: 5.28)
Parks budget requests for new equipment in CB submissions suggest existing maintenance capacity strain
Could indicate contractor or development-related clearing tied to active ULURP applications (254 W 124th, One45, 2395 Frederick Douglass Blvd)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference complaint locations with active construction permits (489 total filings in last 90 days, including 25 new buildings) and ULURP projects
Interview Parks Dept on illegal removal patterns and enforcement response

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints jumped to 7 last week—a 273% spike from the 8-week baseline of 1.9 per week—indicating a sudden environmental concern affecting resident respiratory health last week.
evidence: 7 air quality complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (273% increase, z-score: 4.87)
Spike correlates with illegal tree damage complaints, potentially indicating construction dust or debris burning
25 new building permits filed in last 90 days could be sources of air pollution during demolition/alteration work
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent construction dust, demolition work, or illegal burning triggered complaints; cross-reference with DOB permits
Interview residents on health impacts and contact DEP for air monitoring data

themes_detail.label: Animal Abuse & Unsanitary Conditions
themes_detail.summary: Animal abuse complaints hit 8 two weeks ago (167% above the 3.0 weekly baseline), and unsanitary animal private property complaints spiked to 5 last week (233% above 1.5 average)—suggesting a linked crisis in animal welfare and sanitation over the past 2 weeks.
evidence: 8 animal abuse complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.0 weekly average (167% spike, z-score: 4.08)
5 unsanitary animal private property complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly average (233% spike, z-score: 4.04)
Correlates with broader sanitation breakdown: 1,220 total unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days, plus 496 dirty condition complaints
reporting_angles: Coordinate with ASPCA and city animal control to identify abuse hotspot blocks and response gaps
Document living conditions in complaint locations; interview residents and landlords on enforcement and accountability

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaint Spike
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints surged to 5 two weeks ago—a 233% increase from the 1.5 weekly baseline—indicating a sudden rise in rideshare or livery service violations in Central Harlem two weeks ago.
evidence: 5 for-hire vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (233% spike, z-score: 3.5)
Illegal parking complaints remain high at 1,371 over 90 days, suggesting broader traffic/street management issues
Timing aligns with broader service degradation signals (rodent, sanitation, animal issues)
reporting_angles: Interview TLC and local precinct on enforcement activity; determine if spike reflects increased violations or improved reporting
Map complaints to identify problematic streets and rideshare hotspots
